messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Yes, that’s right. B’s needs should be considered, too. A could buy at market value, or we can discuss another plan that gives each of us a fair share; I haven’t agreed to a discount. I’m fine with all three seeing the same list. We haven’t settled the price or shares.

I’d like to make the house a home for my husband and me. I haven’t settled on a price; by a family discount I mean below market value, but it needs to feel fair to B and C too. I can’t proceed without C’s agreement, and I’m not sure about the will or timing.

Thank you. I’d like my share of the estate to help me get a dance studio started. I’m not sure what amount or timing would be possible, and I don’t have a particular view about keeping the house in the family.

Worth exploring, if the price is genuinely equivalent to what we’d each receive from an outside sale after actual costs—not an extra discount. We still need the will, shares, appraisal and costs confirmed. I haven’t agreed to a purchase.
The list looks right, though please add that I need C’s agreement before we can proceed. I can’t say yet whether we could afford that; we’d need to know the appraisal and the will’s terms first.

The list sounds right to me. Getting cash could help with the studio, but I can’t say whether that idea would work until the will, value, and my share are clear. I don’t have a particular deadline at the moment.
I don’t know who the executor is. I’m willing to ask once we know whom to contact.
Yes. I want a say in choosing an independent appraiser all three of us trust.
I don’t disagree. Those steps seem sensible, and nothing is decided yet.
Yes, I’m willing to choose one appraiser together with B and C.
I don’t know who has a copy or who drafted it.
